十九世紀末，管狀鼓傳入歐洲，西方作曲家開始將其融入交響樂團。十九世紀末至二十世紀: In the late nineteenth century the tubular drum reached Europe, and Western composers began to bring it into the symphony orchestra. From the late nineteenth century into the early twentieth, as timpani technique improved, the tubular drum became standardised and refined. Musical centres such as Vienna and London drove its development and made it an important percussion instrument of the orchestra. By the middle of the twentieth century its design had matured, and it was widely used in classical music, jazz and pop. Today the tubular drum is an internationally recognised standard instrument, adopted in every genre.

管狀鼓主體由優質木材製成，通常採用楓木、橡木或松木等硬質木料製作筒狀共鳴腔，提供: The body of the tubular drum is made of good timber, usually a hardwood such as maple, oak or pine, formed into a cylindrical resonating chamber that gives a stable tonal foundation. The head is natural animal skin such as cowhide or goatskin, which vibrates well. The skin is fixed to the rim with metal or leather lacing, and modern instruments mostly use metal tension rods to tune it. The edge of the rim is usually protected with a metal or wooden hoop, which adds durability and resonance.
管狀鼓在現代管弦樂中應用廣泛。柏遼茲《幻想交響曲》(1830年代)首次在交響樂團: The tubular drum is widely used in the modern orchestra. Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique (1830s) was the first to use a percussion section in a symphony orchestra, which laid the ground for the tubular drum. Dvořák's New World Symphony (1893) takes in percussion of American flavour, including tubular-drum elements. Twentieth-century modernist composers such as Stravinsky used a wide range of percussion in The Rite of Spring (1913), which opened up the tubular drum's possibilities further.
管狀鼓起源於非洲大陸，是膜鳴樂器中最古老的形式之一。早期非洲部落利用樹幹或竹子製: The tubular drum comes from the African continent and is one of the oldest forms of membranophone. Early African communities made a cylinder from a tree trunk or bamboo and covered it with animal skin, using it for communication, ritual and entertainment. The instrument later reached the Middle East and Asia, where each place reworked it according to local custom.
管狀鼓音色深沉渾厚，具有溫暖的低頻特性。其聲音質感介於明亮與暗沉之間，帶有適度的: The tubular drum's timbre is deep and full, with warm low frequencies. It sits between bright and dark, with a moderate resonance. The vibration of the head produces a strong sympathetic response in the cylindrical chamber, which gives the tone more penetration and more layers. Its range is mostly low and low-middle, and it reaches lower than an ordinary shallow drum. Unlike the explosiveness of a drum kit, the tubular drum sounds steady; compared with the heaviness of a bass drum it is more mobile. Its resonance is pronounced and the tail long and full of aftertone. Depending on the diameter and depth of the drum the timbre runs from warm to somewhat rough, which lets it perform well both in the orchestra and in modern music.
膜鳴樂器是指任何主要透過振動的拉伸膜產生聲音的樂器。在原始的霍恩博斯特爾-薩克斯: A membranophone is any instrument that makes sound mainly through a stretched membrane set vibrating. In the original Hornbostel-Sachs scheme of instrument classification it is one of the four great classes. According to Sachs, the sound is produced by a membrane (a "skin" or drumhead) stretched over an opening. Most, though not all, membranophones are commonly called drums. They are classified by material, single or double head, shape, drumhead, the way the head is fixed, the playing position and the way of playing.
